title = {A threshold selection method from gray-level histograms},
journal = {IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics},
author = {Hyndman, Rob J. and Fan, Yanan},

\labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{n} particles were measured in Beispiel\_Partikel.tif (edge-corrected \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{nCorr}); the particles cover \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{areaFrac} of the analysed area. The mean equivalent diameter is \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{meanECD} (standard deviation \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{sdECD}), the mean area \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{meanArea}. The number distribution (Q0) has $D_{10}$ = \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{D10}, $D_{50}$ = \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{D50} and $D_{90}$ = \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{D90}; by volume (Q3), $D_{v50}$ = \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{Dv50}. The mean circularity is \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{meanCirc} (1 is a circle); the mean Feret diameter is \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{meanFeret}. In selection Feld A the mean grey value is \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{roi1Mean} over an area of \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{roi1Area}. In selection L1 the mean grey value is \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{roi2Mean} along a length of \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{roi2Length}.

The micrograph Beispiel\_Partikel.tif \cite{data-image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif} (768\,$\times$\,576 pixels, 16-bit, pixel size \labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{px}) was analysed. Processing comprised, in this order: Subtract background (grey-scale opening, square window, r = 30 px, dark background); Gaussian blur ($\sigma$ = 1.5 px); Threshold (make binary) (Otsu, dark background); Fill holes. The threshold was set automatically with the Otsu method \cite{otsu1979} (\labval{image-analysis-beispiel-partikel-tif}{thr}). Pixels were treated as square. Particles were detected as connected regions of the binary image (8-connectivity) with an area of 2.00 to $\infty$\,$\mu$m$^2$ and a circularity $4\pi A/P^2$ of 0.00 to 1.00. The perimeter is the length of the marching-squares contour between the pixel centres (straight steps one pixel edge, corners cut by half a pixel diagonal), outer contour only (holes filled); the equivalent circle diameter (ECD) is the diameter of the circle of equal area. Only particles whose bounding box does not touch the border of the analysed area were measured; each was weighted after Miles and Lantuéjoul by the inverse fraction of positions in which a box of its size does not touch the border (image $W\times H$, box $w\times h$ pixels: $WH/((W-w-1)(H-h-1))$). Means, standard deviations and D values use these weights; the area fraction includes the particles at the border. $D_{10}$, $D_{50}$ and $D_{90}$ are quantiles of the number distribution (Q0) of the ECD, $D_{v10}$, $D_{v50}$ and $D_{v90}$ of the volume distribution (Q3, weight ECD$^3$, spheres assumed); quantiles by the midpoint rule (for equal weights definition 5 of Hyndman and Fan \cite{hyndman1996}).
